Definition: from G4314 and G2853; to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to adhere:--cleave, join (self).
BiblicalUsage: Proskollao means to glue to, to cleave fast, to join oneself so closely nothing comes between. Jesus quotes Genesis: for this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife, and Paul repeats it as the pattern of Christ and the church.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe cleaving is stronger than leaving: a man leaves one home only because he is glued to another, and Christ is glued to His church the same way.
